# ADR-010. C++ dependencies and reproducibility of the Release build

[Русская версия](../ru/adr/010-build-dependencies.md)

**Status** - Accepted.

**Context.** The services use portable C++ libraries, system media plugins and code generated by Protobuf and gRPC. Build and tests run in Docker on Linux x86-64. Investigating discrepancies needs the exact tool versions, the dependency graph and the ability to repeat the build in a clean directory.

**Options.** A Debian snapshot for all libraries, Conan for the whole graph with an own build of the media stack, or Conan for portable C++ dependencies and Debian for system libraries and related tools.

**Decision.** Conan supplies the Boost and nlohmann/json headers and GoogleTest/GoogleMock for test builds. The GCC and Clang profiles and a common lockfile are part of the repository. Docker prepares the dependencies before compilation. CMake uses CMakeToolchain and the imported CMakeDeps targets. Compilers, GStreamer with plugins, gRPC with Protobuf and their generators, and the storage and cryptography libraries come from a pinned Debian snapshot. The optimized preset builds four executables of the services and the observation source.

**Rationale.** Revisions of portable libraries can be checked and changed independently of a distribution update. A single delivery of the generators and the runtime libraries keeps them compatible. Separate Debug, Release and sanitizer directories prevent mixing objects of these configurations.

**Consequences.** Preparing a new image requires the package sources to be available. A ready image contains the dependencies for compiling without the network. The Conan lockfile pins the versions and recipe revisions. The report keeps the actual identifiers and revisions of the binary packages. A byte-for-byte comparison applies to one source version and one prepared image. [Conan lockfile model](https://docs.conan.io/2/tutorial/versioning/lockfiles.html)

**Verification and review.** `task check:report` checks the matrix, Release and the integrations. When the graph or the toolchain changes, `task build:repro` compares the four executables with an independent compilation in a clean directory. Keep the graphs, the tool versions and the checksums of the core in the regression report. At release, link this information and the SBOM to the hash of the signed kit installed in the release run. Review the delivery boundary when a platform is added, on an ABI conflict, or when a system library version must be supported independently of Debian.
